extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political and moral philosophy (readers of Plato)
extracted.subtask_short: plato's republic on justice and education
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of what constitutes justice, virtue, and the proper education and selection of guardians in both the ideal State and the individual soul. Argues for a tripartite soul/state, role-assignment by nature, and educational methods to harmonize inner parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice in the State (division of labour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The justice of the State consisted in each of the three classes doing the work of its own class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign social roles so that craftsmen, auxiliaries, rulers (or comparable classes) each perform their proper function; this division is a 'shadow of justice' and is essential to the State's well-being. Anti-pattern: class-members doing another class's work undermines justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice in the Individual (internal order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The just man does not permit the several elements within him to interfere with one another, or any of them to do the work of others—he sets in order his own inner life, and is his own master and his own law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate individuals by whether the rational, spirited, and appetitive parts of the soul perform their proper functions without usurpation. Examples: a just person resists allowing desire to rule reason; anti-pattern: internal meddlesomeness leads to injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue as the Health of the Soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is the health and beauty and well-being of the soul, and vice the disease and weakness and deformity of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge moral character by whether practices produce 'health' (order, harmony) in the soul. Good practices lead to virtue; evil practices lead to vice. Analogy: health/disease in body correspond to justice/injustice in soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom (ruling knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: He is wise who has in him that little part which rules, and which proclaims these commands; that part too being supposed to have a knowledge of what is for the interest of each of the three parts and of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wisdom is attributed to the ruling principle when it understands what benefits each part and the whole. Scoring note: assess whether the ruler's knowledge genuinely aims at the interest of entire soul/state rather than factional advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage (spirit obeying reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to be deemed courageous whose spirit retains in pleasure and in pain the commands of reason about what he ought or ought not to fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courage is measured by the spirited element's fidelity to reason's judgments under trials and temptations. Anti-pattern: spirit acting independently of reason (rashness) or spirit failing to support reason (cowardice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance (harmonious agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperate who has these same elements in friendly harmony, in whom the one ruling principle of reason, and the two subject ones of spirit and desire are equally agreed that reason ought to rule, and do not rebel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance is the internal consensus that reason should govern; evaluate by the absence of internal conflict and mutual acknowledgment of roles. Example: a temperate person refrains from desires because the parts agree on reason's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injustice as Internal Strife
rubrics_metrics.description: Injustice is a strife which arises among the three principles — a meddlesomeness, and interference, and rising up of a part of the soul against the whole, an assertion of unlawful authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify injustice by internal rebellion: when appetitive or spirited elements usurp authority or meddle in others' functions. Consequence: leads to intemperance, cowardice, ignorance, and vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role Assignment by Relevant Natural Difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Different natures ought to have different pursuits, but only differences which affect the pursuit in which the individual is engaged matter; trivial differences (e.g., bald vs. hairy) are irrelevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign tasks based on natural aptitude insofar as it affects functional performance. Avoid basing role assignment on irrelevant bodily or social differences. Example: select a physician by physician-like nature, not by unrelated traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Guardians by Shared Qualities (sex-neutral where relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Men and women alike possess the qualities which make a guardian; they differ only in their comparative strength or weakness. Those women who have such qualities are to be selected as the companions and colleagues of men who have similar qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select guardians by capacity and character, not merely by sex. Where duties are the same, education and selection should be equal; allow for individual variation in aptitude. Anti-pattern: excluding women categorically despite demonstrable ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education to Harmonize Soul Parts (music and gymnastic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The united influence of music and gymnastic will bring them into accord, nerving and sustaining the reason with noble words and lessons, and moderating and soothing and civilizing the wildness of passion by harmony and rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combined cultural (music/poetry) and physical (gymnastic/military) education to align rational, spirited, and appetitive elements. For guardians, both sexes should receive music and gymnastic, and where applicable, military training. Practical note: education shapes whether spirit allies with reason or desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirst/Desire Distinguished by Object Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirst is the desire which the soul has of drink, and of drink only; qualified desires arise when additional conditions (heat, cold, quantity) accompany the thirst; simple desire seeks the simple object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing motives, distinguish simple/precise desires from qualified cravings. This conceptual clarity matters when attributing parts of the soul to different motives (appetitive vs. rational). Example: pure thirst vs. thirst for 'good' drink — be careful about conflating universal 'good' with specific appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirited Element's Double Role (ally of reason when educated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Passion or spirit is akin to desire but can be an ally of reason when not corrupted by bad education; it is present early in children and in animals, showing it is distinct from reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether education has cultivated spirit to support reason (desired outcome) or to side with appetite (corruption). Use examples (Leontius' story) to illustrate spirit siding with desire vs. reason. Educational implication: proper nurture can align spirit with rational aims.
